subject: Chemistry
title: Particles Have Spaces Between Them
summary: 50 mL of water plus 50 mL of alcohol gives only about 96 mL. The reason: particles of matter have spaces between them.
keyPoints: Matter is made of tiny **particles with spaces between them**.
When liquids mix, some particles fit into the spaces between others: 50 mL + 50 mL ≈ **96 mL**.
Sugar dissolves because its particles move into the **spaces between water particles**.
Space between particles: **solid < liquid < gas**; gases compress most easily.

blocks.p: Mix **50 mL of water** with **50 mL of alcohol** (ethanol). You expect 100 mL but measure only **about 96 mL**. Nothing spilled.

blocks.alt: 50 mL water plus 50 mL alcohol giving about 96 mL
blocks.caption: The total volume is less than the sum.

blocks.p: All matter is made of tiny **particles**, and there is empty **space between them**. When two liquids mix, some particles of one slip into the gaps between the particles of the other, so the mixture takes up less room.

blocks.alt: Sand filling the gaps in a jar of marbles
blocks.caption: Analogy: sand runs into the gaps between marbles and the level hardly rises.

blocks.p: At Class 9 level the key idea is the spaces; the attraction between water and alcohol particles also pulls them a little closer.
Dissolve a spoon of sugar in half a beaker of water: the sugar vanishes and the level **hardly changes**. Its particles have gone into the spaces between the water particles.

blocks.alt: Sugar particles sitting in the spaces between water particles
blocks.caption: White: sugar particles in the gaps.

sections.h: Spaces in solids, liquids and gases

blocks.alt: Particle spacing in a solid, a liquid and a gas
blocks.caption: Spacing grows from solid to liquid to gas.

quiz.q: 50 mL of water and 50 mL of alcohol are mixed. The total volume is about:
quiz.explain: Some particles fit into the spaces between others, so the mixture is about 96 mL, a little less than 100 mL.

quiz.q: When sugar dissolves in water, the water level:
quiz.explain: Sugar particles move into the spaces between water particles, so they add very little volume.

quiz.q: In which of these are the spaces between particles largest?
quiz.explain: Air is a gas; gas particles are far apart, with the largest spaces.

quiz.q: Why can a gas be compressed much more than a solid?
options: Gas particles have large spaces between them
quiz.explain: The large spaces between gas particles let them be pushed closer together; solid particles are already packed closely.

simulation.reason: One qualitative observation (volumes do not simply add because particles fit into spaces). The video's mixing animation, the marbles-and-sand analogy and the diagrams show it fully; a slider-driven packing model would add little and a quantitative contraction model would mislead at this level.
